competencies.text: Explain Earth's characteristics supporting life versus other planets.

days.title: Why Earth Supports Life
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to explain the unique characteristics of Earth that support life and compare them to other planets in the Solar System.

🌍 Earth — The Only Known Home of Life

Among the 8 planets in our Solar System, only Earth is known to support life. Scientists call Earth's unique combination of features the Goldilocks conditions — everything is just right for life.

🌡️ The 6 Key Conditions for Life

ConditionWhy It MattersEarth's Status
1. Liquid waterAll known life needs water as a solvent for chemical reactions✅ 71% of surface is water; liquid range 0–100°C
2. Suitable temperatureProteins and enzymes work best at 0–40°C✅ Average 15°C thanks to atmosphere + greenhouse effect
3. Protective atmosphereFilters harmful UV and traps heat✅ 78% N₂ + 21% O₂ + trace gases including ozone (O₃)
4. Right distance from the SunNot too hot, not too cold✅ 1 AU (149.6 million km) — perfect zone
5. Stable magnetic fieldDeflects harmful solar wind and cosmic rays✅ Generated by Earth's molten iron core
6. Energy sourceDrives photosynthesis and food chains✅ Sunlight (plus geothermal energy)

🪐 Comparison with Neighboring Planets

PlanetDistance from SunAvg TempAtmosphereLife?
MercuryClosest167°CAlmost none❌ Too hot, no atmosphere
Venus2nd464°C96% CO₂ (runaway greenhouse)❌ Far too hot, crushing pressure
Earth3rd15°C78% N₂, 21% O₂✅ Life thrives
Mars4th−63°CThin CO₂ (1% of Earth's)❌ Too cold, no liquid water
Jupiter5th−108°CHydrogen + helium❌ Gas giant, no solid surface

🌊 The Importance of Liquid Water

Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves more substances than any other liquid. It also:

  • Has a high heat capacity — keeps temperature stable.
  • Expands when it freezes — ice floats, insulating lakes so life survives below.
  • Is a key reactant in photosynthesis (6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂).
  • Transports nutrients and waste in living organisms.

🛡️ Earth's Protective Atmosphere

Earth's atmosphere has layers, each with a job:

LayerFunction
TroposphereWeather, clouds, breathable air
StratosphereOzone layer absorbs harmful UV radiation
MesosphereBurns up meteors
ThermosphereAuroras; ISS orbits here
ExosphereTransition to space

🧲 The Magnetic Field — Earth's Invisible Shield

Earth's magnetic field, generated by its molten iron core, extends thousands of kilometers into space. It deflects:

  • Solar wind — charged particles streaming from the Sun.
  • Cosmic rays — high-energy radiation from space.

Without the magnetic field, solar wind would strip away the atmosphere — as happened on Mars billions of years ago.

☀️ The Sun — Earth's Energy Source

Nearly all energy on Earth comes from the Sun:

  • Photosynthesis — plants convert sunlight into chemical energy.
  • Weather & climate — Sun heats the atmosphere and oceans, driving wind and rain.
  • Fossil fuels — ancient stored sunlight (coal, oil, gas).
  • Solar power — directly converted to electricity.

🌏 The Big Idea

Earth is not just any planet. The exact combination of liquid water, moderate temperature, protective atmosphere, correct distance from the Sun, magnetic field, and abundant sunlight makes Earth uniquely capable of supporting life. This is why our planet is special — and why protecting it matters.

📌 Quick Check

  • Why can't Venus support life? (Answer: surface temperature of 464°C, crushing CO₂ atmosphere)
  • What does the ozone layer do? (Answer: absorbs harmful UV radiation from the Sun)
  • What generates Earth's magnetic field? (Answer: its molten iron core)

days.title: Match Game — Earth's Unique Traits
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each unique characteristic of Earth to its correct description or purpose. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Universal solvent — needed for all known life
Filters UV radiation and traps heat
Absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere
Deflects solar wind and cosmic rays — generated by molten iron core
Correct distance from the Sun — not too hot, not too cold
Surface temperature of 464°C and 96% CO₂ atmosphere — no life
Thin CO₂ atmosphere and −63°C average — too cold for liquid water
Energy source for photosynthesis and weather

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Comparing Planets
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🚀 Scientists are searching for life on Mars. Why is liquid water the KEY factor they look for?

choices.label: B) Because all known life needs liquid water as a solvent for chemical reactions
C) Because water is rare in the universe
D) Because water is easy to find

scenario.text: 🪐 Venus is similar in size to Earth but has a surface temperature of 464°C. What caused this extreme heat?

choices.label: A) It's closer to the Sun, and its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat via a runaway greenhouse effect
B) It has more volcanoes than Earth
C) It has a magnetic field that heats it up
D) It has no atmosphere at all

scenario.text: 🧲 If Earth lost its magnetic field, what would most likely happen?

choices.label: A) Solar wind would gradually strip away the atmosphere

scenario.text: 🌊 Why does ice float on water, and why is this important for life?

choices.label: A) Ice is less dense than water, so it floats and insulates the water below, allowing aquatic life to survive in winter
B) Ice is heavier than water
D) Floating ice has no effect on life

scenario.text: 🌞 Why do we say that nearly all energy on Earth comes from the Sun?

choices.label: A) Photosynthesis, weather, fossil fuels, and food chains all trace back to solar energy
B) Earth has no other energy source
D) Wind is caused by Earth's rotation only

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Planetarium
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Planetarium

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: Which planet is known as Earth's 'sister planet' due to its similar size?
What percentage of Earth's surface is covered by water?
What is the primary function of the ozone layer?
Why is Earth's distance from the Sun called the 'Goldilocks zone'?

choices.label: A) It's not too hot and not too cold — just right for liquid water
B) It's the closest planet to the Sun
D) It matches the color of gold

escape.text: Which planet has the highest surface temperature in our Solar System?

choices.label: A) Venus (464°C due to runaway greenhouse effect)
